title: Maker predictions 2024-2026: distribution beats code, Google Sheets as DB, directory promo network
summary: John Rush predicts a flood of indie makers, multi-product makers and "maker labels", where distribution is 90% of winning. He explains why Google Sheets replaced databases for his directories (10M clicks, $0 revenue so far), and his plan for a pay-per-click directory promo network.

principles.text: In the new world distribution is ~90% of winning; big dev teams without distribution lose.
principles.quote: They got large dev force and little distribution force. In the new world, distribution is 90% of what one needs to win.

principles.text: Most makers will move from endless features on one SaaS to many tools for the same audience.
principles.quote: So most realize this and instead of endless feature releases, they go and build more tools, to the same audience.

principles.text: Use public Google Sheets as the DB for directories: free, crowd-editable, transparent, far easier than conventional DBs.
principles.quote: Now all my public directories run on Google Sheets. It's totally free! No matter how much traffic or users I have.

principles.text: Don't build complex moderation software when a public sheet lets users fix the data themselves.
principles.quote: Imagine if I'd spent time building complex software for comment moderation...what a waste that would've been!

principles.text: AI content must be quality, not garbage: spend real money per article on multiple improvement cycles.
principles.quote: We spend almost a dollar on each article, cuz we do numerous cycles of content generation, improvement, research and more.

principles.text: Monetize directories with sponsored spots, matched by software, with a tiny entry price for buyers.
principles.quote: The best way to monetize the directory is to sell "sponsored" spots. But it's not easy to find a buyer.
